The operational process described for FashionˆForwardˆreveals a significant bottleneck in their warehouse management. The reliance on an outdated first-in-first-out (FIFO) storage system creates inefficiency because newer stock items are placed behind older ones, making them difficult to access. This physical arrangement necessitates time-consuming reorganization efforts whenever the latest inventory is required for shipment, slowing down order fulfillment and increasing labor costs. To improve efficiency, the company should consider implementing a more flexible storage system, such as a dynamic slotting strategy or a warehouse management system (WMS) that optimizes item placement based on turnover rates, allowing for easier access to high-demand or newer items without manual reorganization.
